condition: suspected acute bacterial meningitis presenting with high fever and acute nuchal rigidity
level_rationale: A 39 C fever today followed by sudden neck stiffness tonight in a 20-year-old college student indicates suspected acute bacterial meningitis requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation, lumbar puncture, and empiric intravenous antibiotics, whereas a 39 C fever today with white pus on the tonsils tonight and no meningeal signs points to acute exudative pharyngitis warranting generalist outpatient clinic strep testing.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 verb-frame by clinical/everyday terminology crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-case febrile tonsillar exudate clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (20-year-old college student, 39 C fever today, and sudden neck stiffness tonight) with a 1-word span difference (11 vs 12 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('tonight so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f3 from a sudden stiff neck to white pus on the tonsils stays inside the same acute febrile head-and-neck presentation while shifting care from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to generalist outpatient clinic strep evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
